descriptor.scene: The portal stands open in the green, left-of-center and clear of the exact middle of the frame, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light, vines drawn aside, lower tip floating above the ferns. THROUGH its opening, asked for by name: open morning sky and FOUNDER PARADISE, small and far and sunlit, exactly the silhouette of its locked establishing plate (teardrop of pale rock below, terraced gardens, low cream buildings, slender brass wind-spires), rising into view like a sunrise seen through a window. The island appears ONLY inside the portal's opening, never in the jungle sky. From the right, MAYA, CHRISSY and the ENGINEER walk together toward the light, seen from three-quarters BEHIND, Chrissy a half-step ahead with the warm gold already on her shoulders, Maya with her laptop under her arm, the engineer last with his steady stride; the portal is comfortably taller and wider than all three, room to spare. Warm gold spills over the trail toward them. The lower right corner above the caption card stays calm ferns and warm-lit trail.
descriptor._caption: The portal is warm as a doorway at dusk, and it is still wide enough for every friend who comes. They step through together, out of the green and into the sky, and Founder Paradise comes up like a sunrise.
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
the island anywhere OUTSIDE the portal's opening
a silver ribbon, thread, cable or elevator anywhere
the characters' faces in more than three-quarter-behind profile

No frame, no ring, no arch, no standing stones, no machinery, no doorsill: the light alone is the door. Each era gets exactly one portal, and it shrinks: the more founders pass through and the longer it stands open, the smaller it gets, until it closes and leaves a flat ring of pale gold blossoms on the forest floor. Every portal in every era is this same design at some size. This era's portal at its opening is 3.8 m tall by 2.0 m wide: about twice a person's height, so a founder walks in without ducking and an adult's head reaches only halfway up the opening. Waning, the same shape shrinks to about 1.0 m, knee-to-waist high on an adult. Closed, a flat blossom ring about 2.0 m across lies on the forest floor. The lower tip always floats a hand's width (0.15 m) above the floor. The portal stands still; it never drifts, tilts or hovers higher. State-dependent only. Hidden: hanging vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow curtain the light so only warm slivers show through; a passerby would walk within arm's length and never know. Master (found): the vines drawn aside, the oval open and generous, warm gold light with a few small drifting motes, soft warm glow on the nearest leaves. Waning: the same portal small and low, light gentler, the green closing in around it. Closed: no light at all, a quiet flat ring of pale gold blossoms in the green, moss and ferns grown back inside it. Nothing is ever scorched, broken or ominous. At its opening, about twice a person's height and wider than a garden gate; a closed ring reads about as wide as a person is tall lying down. In a wide shot the live portal is a tall warm almond of light against the green, unmistakably person-scaled, never building-scaled and never coin-scaled. founder-paradise exactly as its reference plate: A floating protopian island in open sky above the jungle. Underneath, a gentle teardrop of pale rock trailing thin skirts of mist. On top, terraced gardens stepping up from the rim, low cream buildings with warm windows, slender brass wind-spires, small orchards and pools. It floats free: no chains, no pillars, no engines. Two fixed camera angles: ESTABLISHING (from below, over the jungle canopy) and TERRACE (standing on a rim garden terrace looking along the edge, jungle far below like a green sea). From below, the island sits high in the frame with canopy or clearing in the lower third; it is never close enough to read individual doors. On the terrace, the rim rail and the drop beyond it carry the height; buildings stay low and behind, sky stays generous. Pale terraced stone, green gardens, low cream buildings with warm windows, brass wind-spires, soft banners without lettering, drifting small clouds. Futuristic reads as graceful and quiet, never chrome, never neon, never engines or thrusters. The island reads about the size of a small hill town: whole gardens and rooftops are visible at once from below, and birds passing near it read as specks. From the terrace, the jungle below reads as a soft green sea with no individual trees.
